hypothesis: Binding friction parity to the deployment-shaped v25 lifecycle diagnostic will remove stale HIP-3 contract mismatch telemetry while retaining per-symbol fee and slippage assumptions and withholding any economic edge claim.
decision: Replace the earlier HIP-3 transfer-experiment execution shapes in report-only friction parity with the exact fixed-80-bps stop, fixed-24-hour hold, no-target shape evaluated by the v25 lifecycle diagnostic. Preserve each symbol's existing modeled fee and slippage assumptions. The refreshed checkpoint reports 24 of 24 routes runtime-shape aligned and zero contract mismatches. Continue to report strategy edge as unidentifiable because only three provider-symbol routes have entry fills and the live closed sample remains insufficient. Keep the armed backend, positions, orders, routes, sizing, and v26 activation state unchanged.
falsifier: The telemetry correction is falsified if a checkpoint from the updated sidecar reports any HIP-3 execution-shape mismatch against unchanged v25 contracts. The economic assessment is updated only by reconciled live fills and closes; shape alignment alone cannot falsify the absence of proven edge.
limitations: Per-symbol fee and slippage assumptions remain provisional until additional venue fills exist.
Runtime-shape alignment does not demonstrate signal quality, profitability, or portfolio robustness.
The sidecar restart was report-only; the armed Python backend retained its existing loaded v25 implementation.
No position, order, route, sizing rule, or execution authority changed as a result of this revision.
